To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

EBNA-2 regulates a subset of cellular genes that are involved in chromatin remodeling and that EBNA-3C is involved in regulating the transcription of a large number of genes, including genes involved in chromatin organization.

EBNA- 1 regulates the transcription of a large number of genes, and that the affected genes are significantly enriched in genes that participate in the regulation of chromatin architecture and transcriptional control.
EBNA-2 and EBNA-3C regulate cellular transcription and that EBNA-3B and EBNA-1 regulate cellular transcription.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transcriptional changes that occur upon EBNA-1 induced B-cell immortalisation.
the identification of cellular genes and pathways that are regulated by the EBV nuclear antigen EBNA-1.
the transcriptional changes that are induced upon EBNA-1 transactivation and the potential cellular targets of EBNA- 1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

EBNA- 1 expression induces a broad rearrangement in the cellular transcription landscape that is likely to be mediated, in part, by the targeting of chromatin remodeling and transcriptional complexes.
EBNA- 1 is a master regulator of the cellular environment and the cellular transcription landscape.
EBV-1 expression in BJAB B cells results in a broad rearrangement in the cellular transcription landscape, and this may be due in part to the direct interaction of EBV-1 with cellular genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of EBNA1 in EBV-negative cells leads to a significant alteration of the expression profile of genes involved in chromatin architecture.
EBNA- 1 expression leads to the activation or repression of genes involved in chromatin remodeling.
EBNA- 1 expression leads to a global transcriptional reprogramming of the cellular environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EBNA- 1 expression induces the transcriptional activation of genes that are involved in chromatin remodeling and the modulation of the cellular transcriptional landscape.

the EBNA-1 protein is able to modulate the transcriptional profile of EBV-negative B cells, which is consistent with the notion that the virus has evolved to manipulate cellular processes in order to promote B cell immortalization.
EBNA- 1 expression may induce a profound rearrangement of the chromatin landscape in EBV positive B cells that is likely to be critical for EBV induced B cell transformation.
